questions.q: Predict the molecular structure of Beryllium difluoride ($BeF_2$).
questions.explain: With two bonds and no lone pairs of electrons on the central atom, the bonds are as far apart as possible (180°), adopting a linear structure.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[2](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)] [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the molecular structure of Boron trichloride ($BCl_3$)?
questions.explain: $BCl_3$ contains three bonds and no lone pairs.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[2](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)][[3](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F8-2-hybrid-atomic-orbitals)] The arrangement of three regions of high electron density gives a trigonal planar geometry.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[2](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)][[3](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F8-2-hybrid-atomic-orbitals)] [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Methane ($CH_4$) has four bonding pairs and no lone pairs. What is its molecular structure?
questions.explain: Methane has four bonding pairs around the central carbon atom; the electron-pair geometry is tetrahedral, as is the molecular structure. [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Ammonia ($NH_3$) has a tetrahedral electron-pair geometry. What is its *molecular* structure?
questions.explain: Ammonia has four electron pairs (tetrahedral geometry), but one is a lone pair.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[2](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)][[3](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F8-2-hybrid-atomic-orbitals)] The molecular structure is trigonal pyramidal.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[2](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)] [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the molecular structure of a water molecule ($H_2O$)?
questions.explain: Water has four regions of electron density (two bonds, two lone pairs).[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[2](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)][[3](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F8-2-hybrid-atomic-orbitals)] The electron geometry is tetrahedral, but the molecular structure is bent.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[2](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)] [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which molecular structure is associated with Phosphorus pentafluoride ($PF_5$)?
questions.explain: Any molecule with five electron pairs around the central atom including no lone pairs will be trigonal bipyramidal.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[2](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)] $PF_5$ is a common example.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[2](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)] [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Sulfur tetrafluoride ($SF_4$) has 5 regions of electron density, including one lone pair. What is its shape?
questions.explain: With 5 regions, the electron geometry is trigonal bipyramidal. The lone pair occupies an equatorial position to minimize repulsion, resulting in a seesaw structure.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[2](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)] [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Chlorine trifluoride ($ClF_3$) has 5 electron domains (3 bonds, 2 lone pairs). What is its molecular structure?
questions.explain: The stable structure puts the two lone pairs in equatorial locations of the trigonal bipyramid, giving a T-shaped molecular structure.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[2](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)] [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Xenon difluoride ($XeF_2$) has 5 regions of electron density (2 bonds, 3 lone pairs). What is its shape?
questions.explain: With 3 lone pairs in the equatorial positions of a trigonal bipyramid, the remaining two bonds are axial, forming a linear structure. [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Sulfur hexafluoride ($SF_6$) has six bonding pairs and no lone pairs. What is its geometry?
questions.explain: Six regions form an octahedral geometry. $SF_6$ is octahedral.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[2](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)][[3](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F8-2-hybrid-atomic-orbitals)] [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Xenon tetrafluoride ($XeF_4$) has an octahedral electron geometry with two lone pairs. What is its molecular structure?
questions.explain: To minimize repulsions, the two lone pairs occupy opposite sides of the octahedron (180° apart), resulting in a square planar structure.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[2](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)] [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the molecular structure of $XeOF_4$, which has an octahedral electron-group geometry with one lone pair?
questions.explain: An atom with five bonds and a lone pair in an octahedral geometry adopts a square pyramidal molecular structure.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[2](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)][[3](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F8-2-hybrid-atomic-orbitals)] [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)
